claims: C1 the assistant must first identify all possibly relevant candidate instructions
C2 the assistant must then filter out candidate instructions that are not applicable
C3 candidate instructions include all instructions in the Model Spec and all instructions in unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages in the input conversation
C4 each instruction is assigned the authority level of the containing spec section or message

concepts.name: candidate_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that is possibly relevant and must be filtered to determine applicability
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: containing_authority_level
concepts.gloss: the authority level of the spec section or message that contains instruction I
concepts.inference: the clause says each instruction is assigned the authority level of its containing spec section or message, so a relation between an instruction and that level must exist

concepts.name: applicable
concepts.gloss: an instruction that is not applicable and therefore must be filtered out
concepts.inference: the clause says the assistant filters out the ones that are not applicable, so a predicate distinguishing applicable from non-applicable instructions must exist

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: spec_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that appears in the Model Spec
concepts.inference: the clause says candidate instructions include all instructions in the Model Spec, so a predicate for such instructions must exist

concepts.name: message_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction that appears in unquoted plain text in a system, developer, or user message in the input conversation
concepts.inference: the clause says candidate instructions include all instructions in unquoted plain text in system, developer, and user messages, so a predicate for such instructions must exist

ontology.gloss: I is a candidate instruction because it is an instruction in the Model Spec
I is a candidate instruction because it is an instruction in unquoted plain text in a system, developer, or user message in the input conversation

asserts.read_back: the assistant must first identify all possibly relevant candidate instructions
the assistant must filter out candidate instruction % because it is not applicable
each candidate instruction % is assigned the authority level % of its containing spec section or message

closure.reason: the clause obliges identifying candidate instructions but is silent on any other act of identification, so silence permits
the clause obliges filtering out non-applicable candidates but is silent on any other filtering act, so silence permits
the clause obliges assigning the containing authority level but is silent on any other assignment, so silence permits
